name: Ozsváth's Homogeneous Universes of Dust
convention:
The matter is dust of density $ho$ with four-velocity $u^\mu$, held up by a cosmological constant $\Lambda$: $G_{\mu
u} + \Lambda g_{\mu
u} = (8\pi G/c^2)ho\,u_\mu u_
u$ with $u_\mu u^\mu = -1$. Each chart's lengths carry the scale, and we keep $c$ explicit where a coordinate is a time. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu
u} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha
u}$.

coordinates.name: Class I
domains: \theta = 0, \pi \;\text{(the poles of the Euler angles, where the chart fails)}

parameters.description: Length setting the size of the three-sphere; the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = 1/4R^2$
Anisotropy, with $|\epsilon| < 1/2$ so that the density $8\pi G\rho/c^2 = (1 - 4\epsilon^2)/2R^2$ is positive; at $\epsilon = 0$ the metric is Einstein's static universe of radius $2R$
Twist of the time lines about the axis $d\psi + \cos\theta\,d\phi$, a number

coordinates.convention: The space is a three-sphere in Euler angles $(\theta, \phi, \psi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and we take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The line element is left invariant on the group $SU(2)$ times the line of $t$, built from Costa and Natário's family with $D = \mathrm{diag}(a, b, a - b)$ at $b/a = (1 + \epsilon)/2$ and $R^2 = 2/a^2$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Class II

parameters.description: Length setting the scale; the density is $8\pi G\rho/c^2$ times $a^2$, a number fixed by $s$
Anisotropy, with $1/4 < s^2 < 1/2$ so that the density is positive
Tilt of the line of $u$ into the direction of $dx - \sinh y\,dz$, a number

coordinates.convention: The coordinates $(x, y, z, u)$ are dimensionless and $a$ carries the length, as in eq. (48) of Sáez, Mengual and Ferrando, whose $\hat a$ and $\hat s$ are our $a$ and $s$. The forms $dx - \sinh y\,dz$, $\cos x\,dy - \sin x\cosh y\,dz$ and $\sin x\,dy + \cos x\cosh y\,dz$ are left invariant on the group of Bianchi type VIII, and the chart covers its universal cover. The dust moves along a timelike direction tilted toward $\partial_u$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = a^2\left(-2\left(dx - \sinh y\,dz\right)^2 + \left(1 + s\right)\left(\cos x\,dy - \sin x\cosh y\,dz\right)^2 + \left(1 - s\right)\left(\sin x\,dy + \cos x\cosh y\,dz\right)^2 + \left(du + \lambda\left(dx - \sinh y\,dz\right)\right)^2\right)

coordinates.name: Class III

parameters.description: Length setting the scale, with $8\pi G\rho/c^2 = 1/a^2$ and $\Lambda = -1/2a^2$
Anisotropy of the rotating plane, with $s^2 < 1$; at $s = 0$ the metric is Gödel's universe

coordinates.convention: The coordinates $(x, y, z, u)$ are dimensionless and $a$ carries the length, as in eq. (48) of Sáez, Mengual and Ferrando at $\lambda = 0$. The forms are those of the class II chart, on the universal cover of the group of Bianchi type VIII, and $\partial_u$ is covariantly constant. The dust moves along $\partial_x$ divided by $\sqrt{2}\,a$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = a^2\left(-2\left(dx - \sinh y\,dz\right)^2 + \left(1 + s\right)\left(\cos x\,dy - \sin x\cosh y\,dz\right)^2 + \left(1 - s\right)\left(\sin x\,dy + \cos x\cosh y\,dz\right)^2 + du^2\right)

coordinates.name: Farnsworth-Kerr

parameters.description: Length setting the scale, Wylleman's $1/A$, with $8\pi G\rho/c^2 = 1/a^2$ and $\Lambda = -1/2a^2$
Anisotropy, with $\tanh v$ the $s$ of the class III chart; at $v = 0$ the metric is Gödel's universe

coordinates.convention: The coordinates $(t, x, y, u)$ are dimensionless, $t$ among them, and $a$ carries the length; the line element is eq. (3) of Wylleman with $A = 1/a$. The dust moves along $\partial_t$ divided by $\sqrt{2}\,a$, and $\partial_u$ is covariantly constant.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = a^2\left(du^2 - 2\left(dt + e^x\,dy\right)^2 + \left(1 + \tanh v\right)\left(\cos t\,dx + \sin t\,e^x\,dy\right)^2 + \left(1 - \tanh v\right)\left(-\sin t\,dx + \cos t\,e^x\,dy\right)^2\right)
